plan: Trim QQQI to 20% to cure concentration and reduce overall risk. Trim SPY to 15% and QQQ to 10% to reduce broad index exposure. Trim CRWD to 5% to reduce single name concentration. Sell SMH, METU, and SOXL to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure and cut positions flagged for exit.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for capital preservation with a realistic target of ~1.5% per month. It significantly reduces leverage and concentration, prioritizing stability and lower drawdown. Expect minimal volatility but also limited upside potential.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to cure concentration and reduce risk. Trim SPY to 20% and QQQ to 10% to reduce broad index exposure. Trim CRWD to 8% to reduce single name concentration. Sell SMH due to its exit status. Trim METU and SOXL to reduce leveraged exposure. Buy TZA at 4% as a new strong scanner setup.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets risk-first growth, aiming for ~2.5% per month. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while introducing a new high-quality setup. Expect moderate volatility and a blend of stability and growth potential.

plan: Trim QQQI to 20% to cure concentration and free capital for higher growth. Add to CRWD to 15% to press a working position. Sell SMH due to its exit status. Add to METU, SOXL, MSFU, MUU, and SPAL to 6% each, leaning into leveraged ETFs for aggressive growth.
aggressive.read: This aggressive growth plan targets ~4% per month by leaning into leverage and concentration. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs, which can lead to substantial gains but also much larger drawdowns. Daily decay and rebalancing of leveraged ETFs are significant risks; strict stop discipline is critical.

plan: Add to QQQI to 30% to increase income exposure. Trim SPY to 15% and QQQ to 10% to reduce broad index exposure. Sell CRWD, SMH, METU, SOXL, and MSFU to eliminate high-beta and leveraged positions, prioritizing low drawdown and reliable income.
income.read: This income plan aims for ~1% per month by prioritizing steady monthly distributions. It significantly reduces leverage and high-beta single names, focusing on income-generating ETFs. While prioritizing low drawdown, distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in market downturns.
